title: NYC Daily Digest
text:
☀️ Good morning, Matthew! It's Monday, November 9, 2026.

🌤️ Weather
Cool and breezy. It's in the upper 40s early this morning (estimated). High 58–61°F, low around 47°F tonight. About a 25% chance of a light shower, mostly this morning, then dry. WNW winds 10–20 mph.
👕 Wear a light jacket or layers. The umbrella can stay home unless you want to be extra safe.

🗞️ Headlines
• After the midterms, Democrats now control both the House and the Senate. Trump is defending Defense Secretary Hegseth as an impeachment push builds.
• The COP31 climate summit opens today in Antalya, Turkey. The U.S. is absent, and the Iran war and Gulf oil disruptions hang over the talks.
• Poland: the gunman in Saturday's Kraków mass shooting, which killed at least six people, has died in hospital.
• Israel: President Herzog has asked Gadi Eisenkot, a Netanyahu rival, to try to form a government after an inconclusive election.
• NYC: Mayor Mamdani announced a $25M expansion of the city's cold-weather response. Separately, a ransomware attack is disrupting Queens Public Library services.

🚇 Getting around
• A train: no service between Rockaway Blvd and Ozone Park–Lefferts Blvd until 5am Monday, Nov 16, because of signal work. Check the MTA app for alternatives.
• 1 train: southbound trains bypass 125 St.
• LIRR: new schedules start today, including midday changes on several branches and track-work timetables between Amityville and Lindenhurst through Nov 20.

🎉 NYC today
• Last day of Canstruction at Brookfield Place (230 Vesey St), 10am–7pm: giant sculptures built from canned food, which is then donated.
• The New York Comedy Festival runs through Sunday, Nov 15, with shows across the city all week.

💡 Nugget
Wednesday, Nov 11, is Veterans Day. Expect the Veterans Day Parade on Fifth Avenue and holiday changes to alternate-side parking and some city services, so plan errands for today or tomorrow.
